text.en: Some children made animal and bird faces on old boxes, cans and bottles. A pig face on a cube with narrow eyes, a puppy face on a cylinder with wide ears, a bird face on a cone with a pointed beak and a cat face on a cuboid with long whiskers. Jaya built a rocket and Devika bought a toy engine, and all of them are made of solid shapes.

Boxes, cans, bottles and cones are solid shapes. The box is a cube, the can and bottle are cylinders, a funnel is a cone and a book-like box is a cuboid. A cube is a special cuboid in which all faces are squares. Look at any solid shape and talk about its faces, edges and corners. A face is a flat or curved surface, an edge is where two faces meet and a corner is where edges meet.
Some shapes have straight edges and flat faces, like a cube and a cuboid. Some shapes have curved parts, like a cylinder, a cone and a ball. A cylinder has curved sides, and a cone has a curved side and a pointed top. When we look from far away we can see only the outline and the larger parts of a shape.
Jaya built a rocket with cuboids, cylinders and a cone on top. We count how many of each shape she used. We say where each shape is: between two cuboids, on top of a cylinder or under a cone. Devika's toy engine has red cylinders, yellow cones, grey cuboids and blue cubes, and we count each kind. Construct and describe game: one child puts three shapes together and tells the order, for example the cylinder is on the cuboid and the cone is on the cylinder, and the others build the same without seeing it.
Let us start with a craft, just like the children in our book. They are making animal and bird faces on old boxes, cans and paper. One child made a pig face on a box. A box like that is a cube, and the pig has narrow eyes. A bottle is a cylinder. On it the child made a puppy face with wide ears. A cone is pointed at the top, so the child made a bird face on it, and the pointed top became the beak. A cuboid is a long box. On it the child made a cat face with long whiskers. Now you try. Bring old boxes and bottles and draw faces on them. Tell us which shape you used for which face.
Let us go on a shape hunt. Look around the classroom for things that look like a cylinder, a sphere, a cube, a cuboid and a cone. Make a table and write the names of the things you find. A duster may be a cuboid, a ball is a sphere, and a chalk box may be a cuboid too. Count each kind. Which shape did you find the most? Which one did you find the least? Tell your friends. Some things are made up of more than one shape. A toy rocket may have a cone on top of a cylinder, so we say it is made of more than one shape.
Pick up a solid shape and turn it slowly. A flat part is called a flat face and a rounded part is a curved face. Which shape has no edges at all? A sphere, like a ball. It has only a curved face. Which shapes have only flat faces? The cube and the cuboid. Which shape has only a curved face? The sphere. Which shapes have both flat and curved faces? The cylinder and the cone. A cylinder has two flat circles and one curved side. A cone has one flat circle and one curved side. Look at a die. It is a cube, so it has six flat faces.
A die has dots from one to six on its faces. Take a die and find the face that is opposite to the face with one dot. The face opposite one dot has six dots. Opposite two dots is five dots, and opposite three dots is four dots. Do you see the pattern? Each pair of opposite faces adds up to seven. One and six make seven, two and five make seven, three and four make seven.
Now let us build. Join shapes to make houses, towers and rockets. Name the shapes you used and say how you arranged them. If you join three cubes face to face, you can make a long straight shape. You can also make a bent shape that looks like the letter L. Try it with blocks. With six dice you can make a cuboid. You can make a tower by putting all six one on top of the other. You can make any shape you like, too. Remember our game. One friend puts three shapes together, tells the order, and the others build it without seeing. For example, the cone is on the cylinder. Well done! Now you can name solid shapes, talk about their faces, and build with them.

problem.en: A toy engine has 2 red cylinders and 3 blue cubes. How many shapes are these in all?

text.en: Count the cylinders and the cubes.
2 + 3 = 5 shapes.

problem.en: Which shape would you use for the top of a rocket?

text.en: The top should be pointed.
A cone has a pointed top, so use a cone.

why.en: The cone is the shape with a point.

problem.en: In the die, the face with 4 dots is opposite which face?

text.en: Think of the pairs that add up to 7.

why.en: Opposite faces of a die always add up to seven.
We need the number that makes 7 with 4.

text.en: The face with 3 dots is opposite.

problem.en: Which shapes have both flat and curved faces?

text.en: Think of a can. The top and bottom are flat, the side is curved.
Think of a funnel. The wide round part is flat, and the sloping side is curved.

why.en: A cone has one flat and one curved face.

text.en: The cylinder and the cone have both kinds of faces.

why.en: A cube has only flat faces and a ball has only a curved face.

prompt.en: Name the shapes you can use to make a house and tell how you arranged them.

requiredIdeas.en: Use words like on top, between and under

commonMisconceptions.en: A cube and a cuboid are never alike

points.en: Boxes are cubes or cuboids, cans are cylinders and funnels are cones.
Shapes have faces, edges and corners.
We describe where shapes are placed with words like on, under and between.
Cube and cuboid have only flat faces; a sphere has one curved face and no edges.
A cylinder and a cone have both flat and curved faces.
Opposite faces of a die add up to 7.
We can join shapes to build houses, towers and rockets, and describe where each shape is placed.
